reconstructed_theorem_text: It is not the case that for every measure mu on the real line and every two functions f and g from the real line to itself, f equals g mu-almost everywhere implies that the classical gradients of f and g are equal mu-almost everywhere.
objects: A measure mu and two functions f and g, together with their total classical gradients.
domains: mu is a measure on the real line; f and g are functions from the real line to itself.
quantifiers: An outer negation scopes over the universal quantification of every measure mu and every pair of functions f and g.
assumptions: Inside the universally quantified implication, the sole premise is that f equals g mu-almost everywhere; no differentiability or other regularity hypothesis is assumed.
conclusion: The universally quantified implication from mu-almost-everywhere equality of f and g to mu-almost-everywhere equality of their classical gradients is false.
scopes: The negation applies to the entire universal implication, and both almost-everywhere assertions are taken with respect to the same measure mu.
constant_dependencies: No numerical constants or source-application parameters occur; the statement depends only on measures, real-valued functions on the real line, almost-everywhere equality, and the total classical gradient.
